Anya K.: Quick Q — what is our current contract for stream keepalives / heartbeats at the edge? trying to reason about how retries + fallback compose when a client stops sending heartbeats.
Mike L.: Short answer: edge expects a periodic heartbeat header or ping frame; if missing for > lease window we consider the client gone. but details fuzzy around retries.
Sam T.: Can you sketch the sequence you're worried about? e.g., client disconnect vs network blip vs server GC.
Anya K.: Scenario: client opens streaming generation -> server replies streaming tokens. network hiccup causes client TCP to drop for ~12s, client TCP reconnects and attempts to re-open stream. meanwhile edge didn't see heartbeat and initiated fallback to a cheaper model variant. when the new client stream appears, do we re-associate state, resume KV cache, or start fresh?
Izzy R.: TL;DR: we currently tie resume to a resume-token bound to the connection lease id. if lease expired, resume is inhibited. That prevents duplicate cost and double-side effects.
Mike L.: Right. But heartbeat contract impacts the expiry delta. Two knobs: keepalive interval (client->edge) and grace period (edge wait before expiring lease). We need clear defaults and a composable retry rule.
Anya K.: Proposal: enforce a minimal `X-Stream-Heartbeat: <ms>` header. Edge uses that as soft hint. If heartbeat stops, start a grace timer = max(3*interval, default-ttl). Only expire after grace. During grace we allow transparent client reconnections carrying same `Resume-Id` to re-associate. After expiry we mark lease "closed" and trigger fallback routing.
Sam T.: I like separate states: ACTIVE -> GRACE -> CLOSED. While GRACE we keep KV cache pinned but deprioritized (eviction allowed after soft cap). That limits memory while allowing cheap resume.
arch-bot: RFC ref: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/stream-resume-2025 (summary: ACTIVE/GRACE/CLOSED lifecycle + resume-token binding).
Mike L.: Need to define how retries interact: client retry should attempt re-open within grace using same Resume-Id. If edge receives a reconnection after grace but before full closed, we should still allow resume iff reconnection includes proof (same resume-token + ephemeral signature). Otherwise we treat as cold start.
Anya K.: What about server-initiated fallback? If fallback kicks in and runs short generation on a lighter model, and a resumed client shows up, do we merge outputs? That seems risky.
Izzy R.: We should avoid merge. Instead: if fallback was taken after lease moved to CLOSED, any resumed attempt must be treated as new request (no merge). If fallback happened during GRACE (i.e., we started a hedged request but kept lease), we can accept resume and prefer the in-flight hedged result if it's compatible. Need compatibility checks (prompt hash + prefix offset).
Sam T.: Implementation sketch (pseudo):
```
on_heartbeat(lease): reset(grace_timer)
on_disconnect(lease): start(grace_timer)
if reconnection and resume_id == lease.resume_id and now < lease.closed_at: reattach_kv_cache() else: cold_start()
```
Mike L.: Also add flow-level metrics: heartbeat-miss-count, resume-success-rate, fallback-triggered-during-grace. These drive tuning.
Anya K.: Ops question: what default numbers? my suggestion: heartbeat interval 10s, grace = 3x interval (30s), closed eviction soft-cap 5 minutes (for pinned KV) then hard eviction 15m. Thoughts?
Izzy R.: Defaults seem reasonable. Need a knob per-customer/tier (premium customers get longer grace / pinned KV retention).
Sam T.: One more: make keepalive pluggable for WebSocket vs HTTP2 vs SSE; provide both header hint `X-Stream-Heartbeat` and an actual ping frame for ws/h2. Edge should treat them equivalently.
Anya K.: Agreed. I'll draft a follow-up RFC with states, headers, example reconnection handshake, and expected metrics. Will include a short compatibility table for resume vs fallback.
Mike L.: Ack. if you throw the RFC in #architecture we can review and tag infra/ops.
deploy-bot: arch-deploy: created draft rfc/keepalive-composition-2102468101 for review.
Anya K.: thanks — will ping once I have the draft link. :thumbsup:
